## Proof

**Claim:** For every $1 \leq p \leq \infty$, the space $L^p(\mathbb{R})$ contains a subspace isometrically isomorphic to $\ell^p$.

**Construction.** Let $E_n = [n, n+1)$ for $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ (or any sequence of pairwise disjoint measurable sets with $|E_n| = 1$). Define a linear map
$$
T : \ell^p \to L^p(\mathbb{R}), \qquad T\big((a_n)_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\big) = \sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} a_n \,\mathbf{1}_{E_n}.
$$
(Using an index set $\mathbb{Z}$ is equivalent to $\mathbb{N}$ for $\ell^p$; one may relabel. Alternatively use $E_n = [n-1,n)$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$.)

Since the $E_n$ are disjoint, the series defines a measurable function taking the constant value $a_n$ on each $E_n$ and $0$ off $\bigcup_n E_n$.

**Case $1 \leq p < \infty$.** Using disjointness and $|E_n|=1$,
$$
\|T((a_n))\|_{L^p}^p = \int_{\mathbb{R}} |T((a_n))|^p \,dx = \sum_{n} |a_n|^p \,|E_n| = \sum_n |a_n|^p = \|(a_n)\|_{\ell^p}^p.
$$
Hence $\|T((a_n))\|_{L^p} = \|(a_n)\|_{\ell^p}$, so $T$ is an isometry.

**Case $p = \infty$.** The function $T((a_n))$ equals $a_n$ on the set $E_n$ of positive (indeed unit) measure, so every value $|a_n|$ is attained on a set of positive measure, and no value larger than $\sup_n |a_n|$ is attained. Therefore
$$
\|T((a_n))\|_{L^\infty} = \operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{\mathbb{R}} T((a_n)) = \sup_n |a_n| = \|(a_n)\|_{\ell^\infty}.
$$
Thus $T$ is an isometry in this case as well.

**Injectivity.** If $T((a_n)) = 0$ in $L^p$ (i.e., a.e.), then on each $E_n$ (which has positive measure) the function equals $a_n$, so $a_n = 0$ for every $n$. Hence $T$ is injective.

**Conclusion.** $T$ is a linear isometry from $\ell^p$ into $L^p(\mathbb{R})$, so its image $T(\ell^p)$ is a subspace of $L^p(\mathbb{R})$ that is isometrically isomorphic to $\ell^p$. This holds for every $1 \leq p \leq \infty$.
